leads.title: City-wide water-carried sewerage in Hamburg and London
leads.why: Planned sewer networks flushed by piped water ended the cesspool city, and became the model copied by towns around the world.
leads.verify: Lindley's Hamburg system after the 1842 fire, Chicago's (1855) and Bazalgette's London main drainage (1859 to 1875), with the ideas behind them (Chadwick's sanitary report, egg-shaped self-cleansing sewers). Sewage treatment, which followed (activated sludge, Manchester 1914), may merit its own record.

leads.title: City life in Formative Mesoamerica
leads.where: Valley of Oaxaca, Maya lowlands and central Mexico
leads.why: Cities became the centres of Mesoamerican politics, craft and religion; Teotihuacan, laid out on a grid, held about a hundred thousand people.
leads.verify: Founding dates and population estimates for the first cities (Monte Alban, c. 500 BCE; El Mirador and Nakbe; Cuicuilco; Teotihuacan), and whether San Lorenzo (c. 1200 BCE) should count as urban.

leads.title: Land-use zoning in German cities
leads.why: Zoning became the ordinary legal tool of town planning in most countries and shaped the modern separation of homes, industry and commerce.
leads.verify: The Frankfurt zoning ordinance of 1891 under Franz Adickes and earlier partial rules in German cities; transmission to the United States (New York, 1916) and Britain; and older building regulations it drew on.

leads.title: Mammoth-bone dwellings on the East European Plain
leads.where: Dnieper and Don basins, Ukraine and Russia
leads.why: Substantial houses with hearths and storage pits let people winter on the open, treeless steppe of the last ice age.
leads.verify: The best-dated built structures (Kostenki 11, Mezhyrich, Mezin, Gontsy) and what they were; and the older or contemporary claims that could take the first place: the brush huts of Ohalo II in the Levant (c. 23,000 years ago), Molodova I, and the disputed Terra Amata huts.

leads.title: Industrialised large-panel housing in France and the Soviet Union
leads.where: Le Havre and Paris, France; Moscow, Soviet Union
leads.why: Factory-made flats rehoused several hundred million people across the Soviet bloc, Europe and later China within a generation.
leads.verify: The Camus system (patent 1948, first blocks at Le Havre) and its licence to the Soviet Union; the 1954 to 1957 Soviet decisions that made panel building the norm; numbers housed. Earlier trials (Liverpool 1905, Frankfurt in the 1920s) and the post-war steel and timber prefabs are the precedents.

leads.title: Monumental stone enclosures in Upper Mesopotamia
leads.where: Gobekli Tepe and neighbouring sites, southeastern Anatolia
leads.why: Foragers quarried, carved and raised multi-tonne pillars before farming, showing that large cooperative building did not wait for agriculture or the state.
leads.verify: Current dating of the earliest enclosures at Gobekli Tepe and the related sites (Karahan Tepe, Nevali Cori); labour estimates; whether the builders were settled; and what, if anything, later Neolithic building owed to them.

concepts.name: Built dwelling
concepts.summary: Constructing a lasting house from gathered materials instead of relying on caves, rock shelters or windbreaks.

concepts.name: Covered urban wastewater drainage
concepts.summary: Covered street drains collected water from the built-up city; bathing-floor and household drains led towards street channels, and settling features supported upkeep.

concepts.name: Factory-prefabricated panel housing
concepts.summary: Housing assembled at its site from factory-made components.

concepts.name: Land-use zoning
concepts.summary: A municipal rule that divides a town into districts and fixes what may be built in each and how densely.

concepts.name: Monumental construction
concepts.summary: Building works far larger than any dwelling, by organised communal labour, for ceremony, burial or display.

concepts.name: City life
concepts.summary: Many thousands of people living densely in one planned or governed place, most of them not farming, served by a surrounding countryside.
